A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, and their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. V2 explicitly redirects some supplementary brain maps to an external repository; their removal from the supplied PDF is identifiable.

before.justification: V1 reports original fMRI and ECoG encoding analyses, linguistic probing, pretraining dynamics, brain-tuning experiments, and random-feature controls in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds another fMRI subject, dimensionality sensitivity tests, joint statistical analyses, and a Llama-target tuning control.

M1.justification: The core encoding procedures, GRIDE estimation, linguistic probes, surprisal estimation, and WavLM layer-9 brain-tuning recipe are retained. Llama-target tuning is introduced as an experimental comparator; the proposed brain-tuning procedure remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same fMRI and ECoG datasets, The Pile, LibriSpeech, and SentEval, retaining the same language, domains, and evaluation tasks. UTS01 expands the existing fMRI sample. The Llama-target control uses existing inputs and evaluations.

E2.justification: V2 Figure H.4 adds WavLM-base-plus tuned to Llama-3-8B representations as a comparison with brain-tuning. The original language and speech models, random Fourier features, and PCA/participation-ratio comparisons remain; participation ratio was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The fMRI sample increases from UTS02–03 to UTS01–03, and principal fMRI results switch from highlighting UTS03 to averaging participants. Added experiments introduce halved/doubled GRIDE scales and a Llama-representation tuning target. These extend the existing design while retaining its datasets, splits, and core training procedures.

E4.justification: V2 adds explicit tests of whether Id peaks and brain-predictivity correlations survive GRIDE-scale perturbations (Tables C.2–C.3, Figure C.2), additional PR-versus-Id cases (Figure C.3), and a control testing whether tuning to another model reproduces brain-tuning effects (Figure H.4). Conversely, seven model-specific brain-map series present in v1 are omitted from the PDF, although summary tables remain.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's pairwise correlations and permutation tests, v2 Section 4.1 introduces mixed-effects regressions jointly estimating Id and surprisal effects, with model grouping, standardized coefficients, and significance results for both modalities. This substantially extends inference about the competing explanations. Figure 5 also specifies SD aggregation across subjects and data splits; five Id bootstraps were already reported in v1.

E6.justification: V2 adds UTS01 results, joint-regression estimates, scale-sensitivity outcomes, and the finding that Llama-target tuning improves encoding and semantic probing without increasing Id. Table 1 replaces UTS03 fMRI results with three-subject aggregates: overall Id correlation changes from 0.76 to 0.72 and surprisal correlation from -0.51 to -0.53. These are different aggregations, not same-setting performance changes; UTS03 values survive in Table H.1. Table G.1 also revises several peak-layer entries.

T1.justification: Appendix C retains the GRIDE likelihood, local-density assumptions, participation-ratio definition, and accompanying mathematical explanation. No new theorem, proof, or substantive formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central account: semantic abstraction explains brain alignment, Id tracks encoding performance across layers and training, and brain-tuning increases semantic content and Id. Added evidence does not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations: Id cannot identify the specific encoded features, and brain-tuning does not establish the full causal relationship. Section 4.1 narrows the rejection of prediction to its role as a primary driver, and Section 4.3 softens causal wording. Appendix C also removes v1's explanation attributing poor linear-dimensionality behavior to massive residual-stream activations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 replaces the promised future code link with a concrete repository address. Appendix A.4 newly documents brain-tuning on A100-equipped nodes and approximately 50 node-hours. V2 also supplies access instructions for supplementary maps moved outside the PDF; the linked resources were not inspected.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused comparison with prior dimensionality-based explanations of brain predictivity, distinguishing nonlinear Id, generic stimuli, and linguistic-structure interpretation. V2 adds Canatar, Elmoznino and Bonner, Schaeffer, Jawahar, and Kauf references, and removes Doimo et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. V2 makes targeted wording corrections, updates author/footer text, adds a Limitations subsection, expands selected explanations, reorganizes the per-subject appendix, and exchanges the order of the random-feature and brain-map appendices.

P2.justification: The appendix displays are substantially reworked: Appendix C gains two tables and two figures and expands its scale-analysis figure; Appendix H consolidates participant panels and adds the tuning control. The nine-model brain-map series becomes two redesigned figures covering three fMRI subjects, with remaining maps redirected externally. Figure 5 adds explicit uncertainty reporting and revised axes.

improvement.justification: V2 directly strengthens assessment of the central hypothesis through GRIDE sensitivity tests, joint Id/surprisal regression, and an informative alternative-tuning control. Explicit causal limitations and concrete code-access information also improve transparency. The net gain is limited by reduced self-contained brain-map evidence and unresolved reporting inconsistencies: Figure 2's caption still reports 0.76 although its plot and Table 1 report 0.72, and strong causal language remains alongside the new qualifications.
